root_cause.text: The `vb2_dma_sg_mmap` function in the videobuf2 DMA scatter/gather allocator fails to set the `VM_DONTEXPAND` and `VM_DONTDUMP` flags on the `vm_area_struct` (VMA), causing a kernel warning in `drm_gem_mmap_obj` when mapping imported dma-bufs.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff adds `vm_flags_set(vma, VM_DONTEXPAND | VM_DONTDUMP);` to `vb2_dma_sg_mmap` in `drivers/media/common/videobuf2/videobuf2-dma-sg.c` to prevent triggering `WARN_ON(!(vma->vm_flags & VM_DONTEXPAND))` in `drm_gem_mmap_obj()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Set VM_DONTEXPAND and VM_DONTDUMP flags on the VMA to prevent improper expansion and core dumping of DMA buffers.
intent_record.what: Added a call to vm_flags_set() to apply VM_DONTEXPAND and VM_DONTDUMP flags to the virtual memory area.
intent_record.how: This prevents the memory mapping from being expanded or included in core dumps during runtime.

grouping_result.intent: Set VM_DONTEXPAND and VM_DONTDUMP flags on the VMA to prevent improper expansion and core dumping of DMA buffers.

relevance_review.reason: The group's core intent is to set the VM_DONTEXPAND and VM_DONTDUMP flags on the VMA, which directly addresses the vulnerability root cause where these flags were missing.

candidates.rationale: The vulnerability is an omission of setting VM_DONTEXPAND and VM_DONTDUMP flags on the VMA. This omission occurs right after the successful mapping check, which is indicated by the 'return err;' statement inside the error handling block.

vuln_statements.explanation: The vb2_dma_sg_mmap function returns the error code without setting the VM_DONTEXPAND and VM_DONTDUMP flags on the vm_area_struct (VMA), which is required to prevent improper expansion and core dumping of DMA buffers.

commit a17ae14766935aaccd7e7629d1ccf980341ffd24
Author: Souptick Joarder <jrdr.linux@gmail.com>
Date:   Mon May 13 17:22:19 2019 -0700

    videobuf2/videobuf2-dma-sg.c: convert to use vm_map_pages()
    
    Convert to use vm_map_pages() to map range of kernel memory to user vma.
    
    vm_pgoff is treated in V4L2 API as a 'cookie' to select a buffer, not as a
    in-buffer offset by design and it always want to mmap a whole buffer from
    its beginning.
    
    Link: http://lkml.kernel.org
bic_trace_step.reason: The `vb2_dma_sg_mmap` function in this commit does not set the `VM_DONTEXPAND` and `VM_DONTDUMP` flags on the `vma` (vm_area_struct) after mapping the pages with `vm_map_pages()`. This leaves the vulnerability present.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function vb2_dma_sg_mmap (lines 235-269) maps memory into the user vma using vm_insert_page but fails to set the VM_DONTEXPAND and VM_DONTDUMP (or VM_RESERVED in older kernels) flags on vma->vm_flags, which is the root cause of the vulnerability.
